params.body:
Shane, with a screenshot of the admin dropdown: "menu items plakken in hun hover state tegen elkaar".

A menu item is a rounded block (`border-radius: 8px`, `padding: 9px 12px`) with no vertical space between it and the next one. As long as nothing is highlighted you do not see it, but the moment one lights up its rounded corners meet its neighbour's edge and you read one continuous smear instead of one raised item.

Two pixels between items is enough to give the hover its own shape. Both menus that use this form get it: the top menu's dropdown and the user menu.

The `!important` on the top-menu rule is not new taste, it is the block it lives in: the bought theme sets `.dropdown-item` at around 18px and wins from a two-class selector, which is why every rule in that block carries one.

Verified: `npm run build` green (lightningcss rejects a broken selector, so the build is the syntax check), and `StylesheetSyntaxTest` plus `BuildContractTest` green, 15 tests and 868 assertions.
params.title: A hovered menu item has its own shape
